article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Morning Brief
article.dek: Huntley is confirmed, the early game kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, and the Value card is back on the Raiders.

items.headline: Sunday is set: Huntley confirmed, early game first
paragraphs: The app's QB row has Tyler Huntley as Baltimore's expected starter for the 1:00 p.m. ET game against the Bengals, with Joe Burrow on the other side. Saturday's downgrade of Lamar Jackson, out with the high ankle sprain, settled this one a day early — there is no game-time call left to wait on.

The day starts earlier than the 1:00 p.m. ET window. The Steelers at Saints game kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, so that number closes first. For the 1:00 p.m. ET games, inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff — that is the moment that settles any last injury question, including Tampa Bay's Baker Mayfield, who the app still lists as the expected starter with a questionable tag.
items.takeaway: Huntley is confirmed and the early game goes first — check the 9:30 a.m. ET number before it closes, and let inactives settle the rest.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Saturday's downgrades stand, Monday has one open name
paragraphs: The Giants head to Houston thinner than they were Friday: tight end Theo Johnson (neck) and safety Jevon Holland (concussion) were both downgraded to out on Saturday. J.J. McCarthy makes his first start for New York shorthanded.

Monday night is nearly set. The Eagles ruled out receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion) and defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen). Running back Saquon Barkley is questionable after returning to full practice Saturday, and tight end Dallas Goedert carries no designation. For Dallas, receiver George Pickens (shoulder) and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) carry no designation after full Saturday practices, while the Cowboys ruled out tackle Drew Shelton, receiver KaVontae Turpin and linebacker Dee Winters.
items.takeaway: Monday's only open name is Barkley, and his call lands with inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Weather: calm and clear in Baltimore
paragraphs: Sunday in Baltimore at the 1:00 p.m. ET window: sunny, 61 degrees, rain chance 0 percent, wind SSE around 2 mph. The day's high is 66.
That is a fact, not a totals edge — nothing in it argues the total either way.
items.takeaway: Calm and clear in Baltimore for the early window; judge the total on its own.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Your three cards Sunday morning
paragraphs: Hit Rate: Steelers moneyline -158 (FanDuel), Steelers at Saints. The model's win probability is 70.5 percent — that is what this card is for, the pick that looks most likely to win. The evaluator EV is -0.005, and that is fine: Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Balanced: Browns moneyline -130 (DraftKings), Browns at Titans. Model win probability 71.9 percent, evaluator EV -0.003. The middle ground: a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor.

Value: Raiders +3.5 -120 (DraftKings), Rams at Raiders. Model win probability 50.5 percent, evaluator EV +0.002. Value is always the model's +EV play, and after sitting quiet Saturday evening it is back on this number. The edge is thin, so your book's price matters — run it through Check before you play it.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate = most likely to win. Balanced = strong without overpaying. Value = the +EV play, back on the Raiders after a quiet Saturday evening.

items.headline: Monday night: the model and the market still disagree
paragraphs: Cowboys at Eagles: the model's expected margin has this about a pick'em, while the market board has Dallas -4.5 at both books. Tanner McKee makes his second straight start for Philadelphia. Nothing in the overnight board closed that gap.
When the model says pick'em and the market says -4.5, don't guess — run your number through Check. Monday game? Monday check.

items.headline: Learn the Game: the hook
paragraphs: (Hypothetical example:) Imagine a game where your team is a 3-point favorite, and your book offers -3 at one price and -3.5 at a better price. That extra half-point is called the hook. If your team wins by exactly 3, the -3 ticket pushes and the -3.5 ticket loses.

What could it mean? The hook is small, but it decides whole tickets on the most common football margin. A better price is not always a better bet if it buys you the hook on the wrong side of a key number.

How to apply it: before you take the prettier price, ask which side of the key number it puts you on. Then type the exact line and price into Check and let the app tell you whether that version is worth betting.
items.takeaway: The hook is the half-point that turns a push into a loss — check which side of the key number your price puts you on.

items.headline: Overnight: totals climbed in Detroit, the Jets shortened
paragraphs: The busy moves came overnight. The Browns at Titans spread shortened from -2.5 to -1.5 at DraftKings. The Packers at Lions total rose from 54.5 to 55.5 at both books. The Dolphins at Jets spread shortened from -4.5 to -3.5 at FanDuel, with the Jets moneyline moving from -225 to -198. The Colts at Vikings moneyline moved from -300 to -330 at FanDuel. The Rams at Raiders spread moved from -3.0 to -3.5 at DraftKings — the same number the Value card is on this morning. The Giants at Texans spread moved from -10.0 to -10.5 at DraftKings.

Totals ticked down elsewhere: Steelers at Saints from 44.5 to 43.5 at FanDuel, Cowboys at Eagles from 44.5 to 43.5 at DraftKings, and Broncos at Cardinals from 43.5 to 42.5 at DraftKings. No spread flipped sides overnight — these are half-point moves and price ticks, not new opinions.
items.takeaway: A busy overnight board with no side flips — half-points and ticks, so your book's exact number is what counts.

items.headline: What didn't move — and the one timing note
paragraphs: The Bengals at Ravens spread is unchanged at -3.0 at DraftKings and -2.5 at FanDuel, price ticks only. The Lions are still -3.5, the Seahawks still -3.0 at FanDuel, and the Steelers at Saints spread is still -3.0.

When the board hasn't picked up a move, or your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel, tap Check, type in your book's line and price — the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

One timing note, and only one: the thing worth waiting for today is inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff, for a game with a genuinely open injury question like Mayfield's. For everything else, if your book's number works right now and Check says bet, bet now — a good number today beats a hoped-for number that drifts the wrong way.
items.takeaway: Inactives are the one thing worth waiting for today; for settled games, a good number now beats a hoped-for number later.

items.headline: Sunday's job: early game first, then the 1:00 p.m. ET window
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, and the Sunday rush moves numbers fast. Start with the 9:30 a.m. ET game, Steelers at Saints, since its window closes first. Then work through the 1:00 p.m. ET window while the numbers are still Sunday morning's numbers — and check inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff for any game with an open injury question.

One more thing, because the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself: settlement is manual, and there is no auto-settle. Log the losers too, not just the winners — that is the only way the record means anything next week.
items.takeaway: Early game first, inactives for the open questions, and log the losers too — the tracker only works if the record is honest.
